uspat:OutgoingDocument.uscom:P: In re Application of
Aguiar Marcano, Reinaldo Javier
Application No. 19/559,972
Filed: March 7, 2026
For: Method and System for Communication via Passive Reflection from Non-Cooperative Orbiting Objects
: DECISION ON PETITION

This decision is in response to the “PETITION TO THE DIRECTOR UNDER 37 CFR § 1.183 TO SUSPEND PROSECUTION ON CONSTITUTIONAL DUE PROCESS AND NATIONAL DEFENSE GROUNDS [REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESSING],” filed August 2, 2026.
The petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is DISMISSED.

Petitioner is given TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this decision to reply. Any reply should be entitled "Request for Reconsideration of Petition Decision Under 37 CFR 1.183." Any extensions of time will be governed by 37 CFR 1.136(a). This is not a final agency decision within the meaning of 5 U.S.C. § 704. No additional petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f) is required.
37 CFR 1.183 states:

In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations in this part which is not a requirement of the statutes may be suspended or waived by the Director or the Director’s designee, sua sponte, or on petition of the interested party, subject to such other requirements as may be imposed. Any petition under this section must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(f).

The Office acknowledges receipt of the required petition fee set forth at 37 CFR 1.17(f). Petitioner, however, fails to sufficiently identify a specific rule for which waiver under 37 CFR 1.183 is sought. In this regard, petitioner herein requests that the USPTO Director:

uscom:OL.uscom:LI: Find that an extraordinary situation exists under 37 CFR § 1.183 where the interests of justice and the constitutional protections of the Fifth Amendment require the waiver of non-statutory administrative rules;
Grant immediate expedited processing of this Petition on National Defense and Aerospace procurement grounds;

Waive the strict response deadlines for any outstanding pre-exam notifications, including the Notice to File Missing Parts, formally reset the notice commencement date to July 30, 2026, and order a complete refund of all extension-of-time fees, late filing fees, and the petition filing fee paid concurrently herewith;

Order a six-month administrative suspension of all prosecution under 37 CFR § 1.103(a), to be renewed upon request if necessary, to protect this application from procedural dismissal or abandonment; and

Direct that all electronic notifications and correspondence in this application be routed to Applicant and Petitioner's secure registered email address (reinaldo.aguiar.marcano©) isbn9781971481296.com) to bypass the physical mail block.

uspat:OutgoingDocument.uscom:P: With respect to 1., the petition is dismissed. Petitioner fails to identify any specific “non-statutory administrative rules” for which waiver is sought or establish the existence of an “extraordinary situation” within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.183 that prevents applicant from complying with any “non-statutory administrative rules” for which waiver is sought.

With respect to 2., the petition is dismissed. Petitioner has failed to seek relief pursuant to 37 CFR 1.182 with respect to expedited treatment of the instant petition. Petitions filed before the Office of Petitions are, in general, treated in the order in which filed. Expedited treatment of a petition requires a petition and fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.182. A petition to expedite under 37 CFR 1.182 will only be considered at the courtesy of the Office of Petitions when and if deemed advisable.

With respect to 3., the petition is dismissed. The petition generally requests that the time period set for reply to any and all pre-examination Notices be waived with respect to this application. Petitioner, however, does not cite a specific rule for which waiver is sought nor has petitioner established that a “extraordinary situation” within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.183 prevents applicant from adhering to USPTO time periods for reply. Moreover, the time periods for reply to Office communications are not subject to waiver and the adherence thereto is required to avoid abandonment of an application. See, 37 CFR 1.135. Be it further advised that submission of a petition does not stay the time period for reply to an outstanding Office communication. See, 37 CFR 1.181(f).
Petitioner is reminded as a courtesy that failure to timely submit a proper reply to the Notice to File Missing Parts issued August 18, 2026 will result in the abandonment of the application.

With respect to 4., the petition is dismissed. Wherein petitioner requests a six-month suspension of prosecution pursuant to 37 CFR 1.103(a), the application is not currently under prosecution as the application remains under pre-examination. Therefore, the provisions of 37 CFR 1.103(a) are not applicable at this time. To the extent that applicant seeks deferral of examination, petitioner’s attention is directed to 37 CFR 1.103(d).

With respect to 5., be advised that correspondence concerning this application is properly directed to the correspondence address designated by applicant on filing. To the extent that applicant wishes to update their correspondence address, applicant is required to comply with the procedures for so doing that can be found at MPEP 601.03.

Wherein petitioner seemingly seeks to have correspondence transmitted to applicant electronically rather than via USPS, applicant is required to avail themselves to the eOffice Action Program. For further information, petitioner’s attention is direction to the following:
https://www.uspto.gov/patents/apply/checking-application-status/e-office-action-program

Be advised that all future communications concerning this application will continue to be directed to the correspondence address of record until such time as proper instruction to the contrary is received.
